title: Traffic threshold playchart and decision brief (Apr 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact playchart for traffic thresholding, a lightweight decision lattice for day-of release choices, and an annotated draft of release notes for the upcoming April deploy. Intended to be a field reference for deployment leads and on-call engineers. Keep short: actionable checks and explicit trigger points.

Context and constraints:
- Target rollout: Hosted API (models v3.1) and Dedicated pools (pool-17).
- Risk vector: memory pressure on 8xA100-80GB nodes and sudden P95 latency regressions when active prefix caching warms up.
- Primary SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 220ms for lightweight prompts; error rate < 0.5% overall.
- Canary window: 30 minutes at 2% traffic, then 3x increments to 10% if all checks pass.

Quick reference decision lattice (compact):
- If p95 increases by > 35% vs baseline (5m rolling) for 5+ minutes -> pause ramp, remediate (see remediation bullets), re-run smoke tests. If persists > 20 minutes -> rollback to v3.0.9.
- If 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes OR concurrent request queue depth > 250 on any host -> immediate traffic cut by 50% to canary/backpressure lane and escalate to SRE.
- If GPU mem fragmentation leads to OOM on any instance -> immediate rollback for that pool; divert traffic to other regions (auto-fallback) and open SEV-2.
- If error conversion (server->client) spikes but tokens produced per request unchanged -> isolate by model variant (quantized fallback) for 1h trial.

Day-of rollout calendar (local times assumed UTC):
- 08:00 - Prep: Final artifact push done, canary tag created, infra-green verified, ops Slack channel #release-telemetry open.
- 08:30 - Smoke (dry-run): run synthetic smoke against staging with 10k token burst, verify KV cache hit-rate and cold-start latency < 120ms.
- 09:00 - Canary start: route 2% traffic to canary for 30m. Continuous monitoring: p50/p95, 5xx, queue depth, GPU mem usage, K/V cache hit % (per-model).
- 09:30 - Canary review checkpoint: if all green (see canary pass checklist), move to 6% for 20m. Otherwise pause and execute remediation.
- 09:50 - Ramp to 10% for 30m (if previous ok).
- 10:20 - Nightwatch: ramp to 25% and keep 60m observation before broad rollout.
- 11:30 - Broad rollout decision: execs and SRE signoff (+15 minutes consideration). If yes -> staggered 10% increments each 10 minutes until 100%.

Canary pass checklist (must be explicit green):
- p95 delta < 20% vs baseline and absolute p95 < 250ms.
- 5xx < 0.3% and 4xx behavior unchanged.
- GPU memory free margin > 15% on all canary hosts.
- KV cache hit-rate >= expected baseline (warmup allowance 7-12%).
- Traces sampled show no increased tail-latency correlation with specific input lengths.
- No new unique exceptions in logs at rate > 0.1/min.

Remediation quick actions (ordered, minimal blast radius):
1) Pause ramp and roll traffic back to previous tag for the affected pool.
2) Trigger targeted canary rerun on a smaller subset (1 instance) with increased tracing.
3) Toggle model-variant fallback (quantized variant) for up to 1 hour; observe quality metrics.
4) If latency continues, reduce batch sizes on serving runtime (config: batch.max_tokens -> -20%) and re-evaluate.
5) If memory OOMs reported, restart affected hosts with upgraded kernel param (vm.max_map_count -> +50%) as temporary mitigation, escalate to infra.

Communication plan (short):
- On any pause/rollback: release lead posts in #release-telemetry with subject "[ROLLBACK] <service> <tag> reason" and brief steps taken.
- Pagers: alerting escalates to on-call SRE (primary), then release lead, then head of infra.
- Post-deploy: 1h summary posted in Confluence and #release-telemetry, 24h annotated release note emailed to stakeholders.

Short checklist: preflight (30m before)
- Artifact verification: checksum, provenance, release tag verified.
- Telemetry hooks: sampling rate 1% -> 5% for first 60m.
- Tracing: temp higher-sampling enabled for canary hosts.
- Rollback artifact pinned and rehearsal plan verified.
- On-call contact list confirmed.

Post-deploy observation and validation (first 2 hours):
- 0-30m: watch synthetic probe (1m cadence), verify no 5xx spike.
- 30-60m: manual poll of top 5 slow traces.
- 60-120m: compare real-user latencies across regions; check customer-critical routes sample.

Draft release notes (to be edited for public-facing):
- Release: platform v3.1.0 (models + runtime improvements)
- Highlights: reduced small-prompt median latencies by ~10% for common prompts; improved KV cache warmup consistency; added a quantized model variant to reduce memory usage on dedicated pools.
- Developer-facing notes: new config knobs for batch.max_tokens and cache.prefix_ttl; improved kernel selection heuristics for longer contexts.
- Known issues (short): intermittent p95 tail in specific prefix-heavy workloads during cold starts; observed memory fragmentation on 8xA100 configs under heavy mixed-concurrency tests.

Follow-ups and owners:
- Telemetry tuning: Evan Morales -> tune sample rates and dashboards (ETA 2d).
- Memory fragmentation investigation: Priya Srinivasan + Infra -> reproduce with synthetic workload and propose kernel/hotpatch (ETA 1 week).
- Post-release quality report: Rhea Kapoor -> 24h and 7d reports.

Open questions / notes to team:
- Should we include canary-region diversification by default? (pro: reduces correlated infra risk; con: increases complexity on fallback).
- Is the 25% hold for 60m conservative enough for Dedicated customers?

Appendix: quick rollback commands (ops):
- k8s: kubectl -n inference set image deploy/platform-serving serving=image:v3.0.9 && kubectl rollout status deploy/platform-serving
- Traffic cut (gateway): curl -X POST https://internal-gateway/traffic-cut -d '{"service":"platform","percent":50,"to":"stable"}'

This is a living note — update the decision lattice with real observed thresholds after the first two canary rollouts.
